38	---
39	
40	## 1. Diagnose a server ("can't connect", "is it healthy?") — ✅
41	
42	**Frequency:** the single most common request (~34 direct, plus most ticket investigations). Representative: *"customer said they pointed their domain here but its not working"* (08-30), *"cant connect to this minecraft server cmuo7ajqt0rpohl44gj8triev"* (10-01), *"he says he still cannot connect, please do a deep audit"* (09-23), *"is everything running healthy after the reboot?"* (09-13).
43	
44	**Manual procedure (AI):** look up the row in Postgres → `qm status` / Proxmox API on the right node → guest agent ping → SSH in (password or management key) → `systemctl status <game>`, `docker ps`, `ss -lntup`, `journalctl` → `iptables -t nat -S NXEON_FWD` on the owning node (or via the node agent) → `nc`/probe from outside → `dig` A/SRV → check recent jobs → explain. Typically 10–30 tool calls and a few minutes per ticket.
45	
46	**Portal:** `/admin/ops/servers/<id>` → **Diagnose** (also embeddable via `ServerOpsPanel`). One ADMIN_OPS job gathers, in the worker:
47	- DB row + last 7 days of jobs (in-flight + failures), provision error/step;
48	- node API reachability, node CPU/RAM;
49	- VM existence on the recorded node, power state, uptime, CPU/RAM, `ipconfig0` vs `Server.ipAddress`, guest-agent ping;
50	- the server's expected DNAT rules (same `planNatRules` the real sync uses) vs the node's live chain (local iptables on the primary, node agent elsewhere);
51	- guest over SSH: load, RAM, root disk, failed units, OOM kills (24h), game unit + `is-active`, container restart count, last 80 journal lines → highlighted errors;
52	- join port bound inside the guest (any netns, same `gamePortBoundInGuest` provisioning uses);
53	- outside probe of SSH (banner) and the join port (TCP connect / UDP with in-guest confirmation) on the public address; flagged as *hairpin* when probing a primary-hosted server from the primary itself;
54	- subdomain A/SRV via public resolvers (1.1.1.1 / 8.8.8.8) vs `resolveGameServerDnsTarget`; customer's own domain A record.
55	
56	`lib/admin-ops/diagnose-rules.ts` (pure, unit-tested) turns that into a verdict (healthy / degraded / down / unknown), a headline, **ranked probable causes with evidence**, the raw checks, and **one-click fixes** through existing paths: start/reboot (`serverAction`), reconcile (`reconcileServerFromProxmox`), restart game service (`gamePower`), NAT re-sync (`SYNC_FORWARDS`), DNS re-sync (`SYNC_GAME_DNS`), retry provisioning (`retryProvision`), open the job queue, open guest logs. When everything is green the headline gives the exact connect address and says the problem is client-side.
57	
58	**Not covered / limits:** a true probe *from another node* needs a probe endpoint on the node agent (follow-up); today the outside probe runs from the primary. Per-server firewall rules are not yet evaluated rule-by-rule (the `blocked_path` cause points at them).
59	
60	## 2. Power: restart / reboot / start / stop — ✅
61	
62	**Freq.** ~32 (*"go ahead and restart it"*, *"reboot it"*, *"turn the free mc server back on on node 2"*, *"stop this vm, hes overdue"*, *"all servers need to be booted back up … if there is ever a restart"*).
63	**Manual:** `qm start/stop/reboot <vmid>` on the right node, or a DB-inserted job.
64	**Portal:** existing Start/Stop/Reboot on the server page (unchanged), Diagnose fixes, and **Bulk actions** (`/admin/ops/fleet`) with a concurrency cap (1–8, default 2) — the worker's `bulk_power` op releases the next server only when one finishes, skips (and reports) ineligible servers, persists progress so a worker restart resumes. "Boot everything after a node reboot" = Bulk → Start on all STOPPED servers of that node.
65	
66	## 3. Dedicated IP: assign / reassign / release — ✅ (same node) · 🔗 cross-node
67	
68	**Freq.** ~28 (*"assign the IP"*, *"give me a dedicated ip from the singapore pool"*, *"assign them both dedicated IPv4 address"*, *"just do the fucking transfer… is it attached to his server now"*, *"the IPv4 assigned to the node three test server was just a test IP … take that IPV4 and bring it over"*).
69	**Manual:** pick a FREE pool row, OVH/Hetzner vMAC, `qm set --net0 … --ipconfig0 …`, power-cycle, fix `Server.ipAddress/sshPort`, NAT resync, DNS resync, tell the customer. The older admin "release IP" button only freed the DB row and left the VM configured with the address.
70	**Portal (IP & placement card):**
71	- **Give IP to another server (same node)** — dry-run plan + warnings (downtime, billing), typed confirmation (the IP), reason. Worker `ip_reassign`: stop source → release (vMAC removed) → source onto NAT (new private IP + SSH port + game join forwards) → claim *that exact address* for the target (`allocateDedicatedIp(..., { preferAddress })`) → net0/ipconfig0 → power-cycle → restart source → NAT + DNS resync → notify both owners. The target is held by a HOLD job so nothing else runs on it meanwhile. Never auto-retried; each step idempotent.
72	- **Release IP (→ NAT)** — the correct version of the old release button.
73	- **Assign a pool IP** — first free or a specific FREE address on the node; checkbox for whether the add-on is billed at renewal.
74	- **Move to another node** — calls `requestVmMove` (stub until `feature/vm-node-migration` lands — that branch owns cross-node moves and IP carry-over).
75	
76	## 4. Ticket replies — 🔜 (stays with AI)
77	
78	**Freq.** ~26 (*"draft me a reply"*, *"give me ticket reply"*). Memory rule: never send without sign-off. This is language work, not an operation; the Diagnose result (headline, connect address, evidence) is the factual input a human or AI uses to write it. Canned replies already exist.
79	
80	## 5. Renewal price / billing corrections — 🟡 · 🔗 BILL
81	
82	**Freq.** ~20 (grandfathered price, add-on totals, "renew now", "his renewal price should be $8.99, next month 20% off"). Existing tools on the server page (grandfather price form, Renew now, Extend). The ops console links there and adds credit/refund/extend with reason + notification. Stripe/renewal internals are owned by the BILL workstream; nothing here edits `lib/stripe.ts` / `worker/billing.ts`.
83	
84	## 6. Migrate a server to another node — 🔗
85	
86	**Freq.** ~16 (*"migrate their server to node 4 … services, port forwards, dbs, files"*, *"move this customer's entire server onto node 3"*, *"migrate the free mc server to node 2 … porting, sub domains, DNS"*). Owned by the VM move engine branch. The ops console exposes it via `requestVmMove({serverId, targetNodeId, dryRun, reason})` (single server and from the drain planner); today it returns "engine not merged".
87	
88	## 7. Stuck / failed jobs — ✅
89	
90	**Freq.** ~16 (*"this apply game server settings stuff is stuck"*, *"im pretty sure its stuck, please wake it up"*, *"run the cleanup and restart the worker"*).
91	**Manual:** SQL on `Job`, sometimes restarting the worker.
92	**Portal:** `/admin/ops/jobs` — Active / Stuck / Failed / All views, per-server filter, live refresh. Re-queue (FAILED only), Cancel (QUEUED only), Force-fail (RUNNING only after 30 silent minutes) — each with a reason, compare-and-swap on the status, audit row. Policy (`lib/admin-ops/job-queue.ts`, tested): money-bearing jobs (RESIZE, DISK_EXPAND, ASSIGN_DEDICATED_IP) are never re-queueable (their failure is refunded); PROVISION goes through Retry provisioning; cancelling a DELETE un-strands the server (ERROR + note → Reconcile).
93	
94	## 8. DNS / subdomain / custom domain — ✅
95	
96	**Freq.** ~15. Diagnose compares public DNS to the expected target and offers **Re-sync subdomain DNS**; a customer-domain mismatch is flagged *customer-side* with the right value to give them (and the NAT caveat that a bare domain can't carry a port).
97	
98	## 9. Free server / credit / extend — ✅ · 🔗
99	
100	**Freq.** ~14 (*"apply the credit and send it"*, *"extend his trial by a day"*, *"Give Thorabin a Terraria Server… free for 30 days"*).
101	**Portal (Customer ops card, `/admin/ops/customers`):** wallet credit/debit (wraps `adjustBalance`), extend/shorten term (wraps `adminExtendServer` — gifted days never prorate into refundable credit), make free/paid (wraps `adminSetServerFree`). Reason mandatory; optional in-app notification and/or email (generic notification template). Granting a *game* server on a chosen node for N days is the partner-grant workstream (C); VPS grants stay at `/admin/grant`.
102	
103	## 10. Comp resource upgrades — 🔜
104	
105	Existing resize/disk-expand flows charge the customer; a "comp" (no-charge, renewal unchanged until next term) option needs a money-path change owned by BILL. Logged as follow-up.
106	
107	## 11. Tear down test VMs — ✅
108	
109	**Freq.** ~11 (*"tear these down minecraft-o3nu1n, minecraft-nsrtzj"*, *"Yes, destroy all 3"*, *"are you tearing down the old game test servers?"*).
110	**Portal:** Bulk → Delete, fenced to servers owned by staff accounts or accounts excluded from revenue (the owner's/test accounts); typed `DELETE <n>`. Leftover VMs without rows are handled by the drift scan's orphan cleanup.
111	
112	## 12. Refunds — ✅ (wraps `refundPayment`; card when traceable, else wallet).
113	
114	## 13. SSH / root password — ✅ diagnose · existing reset
115	
116	**Freq.** ~9 (*"I reset their root password… now it says I can't connect"*, *"is the ssh password the same?"*). Diagnose shows whether the *platform* can log in and whether sshd answers from outside; guest tool **SSH daemon** shows sshd state + recent auth failures. The owner explicitly does not want passwords reset as an automatic fix, so it is never suggested; the existing reset button remains on the server page.
117	
118	## 14. Node health / resources — ✅
119	
120	**Freq.** ~7 (*"what server is using the most resources"*, *"primary node is becoming unresponsive"*). Diagnose reports node CPU/RAM; guest tools **Top processes (CPU/RAM)**, **Largest files**, **Disk usage**; the drain planner shows committed-RAM % per node before/after.
121	
122	## 15/19. Orphans, drift, templates — ✅
123	
124	**Freq.** ~11 combined (*"do we have any free IPs that aren't being used by deleted or expired servers?"*, *"all ips that become orphaned need to be auto released to the pool"*, VMID reuse incidents).
125	**Portal:** `/admin/ops/fleet` → **Run drift scan** (worker `drift_scan`, read-only): orphan VMs (prod-tagged, no row — staging and untagged infra VMs never flagged), unmanaged VMs (info), missing VM, VM on the wrong node, DB-vs-Proxmox status mismatch, stranded PENDING/PROVISIONING/DELETING rows with no job, duplicate vmids across nodes, IP pool orphans/conflicts/mismatches, missing templates per provisioning node. Safe fixes only: destroy a **stopped** orphan (typed vmid; worker re-verifies tag/state/no row; `destroyVmIdempotent`), release an orphaned IP (refused if any server holds the address or a live DNAT targets it), reconcile status, diagnose.
126	
127	## 16. Logs — ✅ Guest tools: service journal, container logs, game unit status, cloud-init, kernel OOM.
128	
129	## 17. Transfer a server to another account — ✅
130	
131	Moves Server + volumes, websites, DBs, apps, cron, SSL to the new owner; invoices/history stay; optional root-password rotation; typed hostname confirmation; both owners notified.
132	
133	## 21. Node drain / rebalance — ✅ planner · 🔗 execution
134	
135	Pick a node → plan (drain fully or down to a committed-RAM target, same region first, 10 % headroom, largest first, dedicated-IP servers flagged) → "Stop new provisions" toggle (existing `setNodeAcceptsProvisions`) → per-move button calls the VM move engine.
136	
137	## 22/23. NAT gaps, restart game container — ✅ (Diagnose NAT check + resync; **Restart game service** = existing GAME_POWER, VM untouched).
138	
139	## 24–26. Resend emails, SSL reissue, Proxmox ACL — 🔜
140	
141	Low frequency and owned elsewhere (B adminmail owns EmailLog; SSL has its own flow; node ACLs live in Q's onboarding scripts).
142	
143	---
144	
145	## Safety model (applies to every action above)
146	
147	- `requireArea("fleet")` (ADMIN) for server/fleet ops, `requireArea("billing")` for money ops; refused while impersonating. Proven structurally by `test/admin-ops-actions-guards.test.ts`.
148	- Mandatory reason (4–300 chars) on every mutating op, written to `AuditLog` alongside the admin id and target.
149	- Destructive ops require a typed confirmation checked **server-side** (IP address, vmid, hostname, `ACTION <n>`).
150	- Remote work only in the root worker (`ADMIN_OPS` jobs); the web process never mutates Proxmox/iptables.
151	- Read-only ops (diagnose, guest commands, drift) never block on a wedged server job and run in parallel (`adminOpsLockKey`).
152	- Guest commands are a fixed whitelist with allowlisted, single-quoted parameters; output capped at 64 KB and scrubbed of the root password.
153	- Mutating ops are not auto-retried; each step is idempotent and re-runnable after a Diagnose.
154	- SANDBOX (`NXEON_SANDBOX=1`): diagnose returns a labelled simulation, IP ops swap DB rows only, destroys are no-ops.
155

s += """

## Admin server & customer pages redesign (2026-10-01, branch `feature/admin-servers-clients-redesign`)

**Why.** Owner: "the client and server pages in the admin portal are a mess, a lot of potential features/actions/info missing — IP assignment, transfer to a different node/region, apps, docker, firewall, files, db, ssh, literally everything." Both detail pages were single long scrolls that loaded everything (live Proxmox stats, renewal quote, 25 jobs…) on every view and exposed only a fraction of what the platform can already do.

**Rule kept:** nothing that was on the old pages disappeared — every card/control moved into a tab (old `?tab=` style deep links such as `firewall`, `ssh`, `jobs`, `delete`, `invoices` resolve via aliases in `lib/admin-server/tabs.ts`).

### Server page — `/admin/servers/[id]`
- **Shell** (`app/admin/servers/[id]/page.tsx`): header (label/hostname, status, VMID, plan, node/region, owner, in-flight job pill, *Customer view* + *Diagnose* links), URL tab bar (`components/admin/server360/TabBar.tsx` — real links, ←/→/Home/End keyboard nav, `.adm-subtab` styling), only the active tab renders, streamed behind `PanelSkeleton`. Core row loaded once via React `cache` (`components/admin/server360/core.ts`).
- **Overview** — *State truth*: DB status vs Proxmox (live, 6 s cap via `lib/admin-server/live.ts`) vs `GameRuntime`, side by side, with every disagreement listed by severity (`lib/admin-server/state-truth.ts`, pure + tested: DB RUNNING/VM stopped, suspended-but-running, VM missing on node, game crashed with run intent, stuck transitions, stale probes; an unreachable node is never reported as a mismatch) and the existing one-click fix (`applyFix`: reconcile, start, restart game, NAT resync). Placement & plan, live CPU / guest RAM + disk samples / uptime / net, owner card (+impersonate), billing summary, quick power/suspend.
- **Network** — addresses (public/SSH/private/IPv6), dedicated-IP rDNS (`adminSetReverseDns`), the Admin Ops IP card (assign / release→NAT / reassign with dry-run plans + typed IP), port forwards with add/remove and conflict detection (`lib/admin-server/network.ts`), NAT chain card (node chain, port range, last fleet resync, resync button — live iptables is not read here), subdomain/custom domain + change + DNS resync, platform firewall rules (add/toggle/delete), guest firewall + listening ports read-only via allowlisted guest commands.
- **Access** — SSH host/port/command, management-key presence, **audited root-password reveal** (reason required; AuditLog `admin.server.credential_reveal` with admin, IP, reason — never the secret; recent reveals listed), password reset (existing), owner's SSH keys, SSH login/failed telemetry, VNC console, web terminal link, impersonate.
- **Compute** — power, entitlement, live VM config (secrets filtered) with pending changes, memory/balloon policy verdict (`pinVerdict` from the pinning code, policy + RAM-guard mode), snapshots list + take/rollback/delete (typed name), volumes, reinstall (typed hostname; same image → REINSTALL job, other image → `reinstallToOs` with its minimums). Honest notes: admin comp-resize and rescue mode do not exist yet.
- **Software** — read-only discovery (docker containers incl. compose labels, failed units, top CPU, listening sockets), common systemd services with audited start/stop/restart, websites, SSL certificates, databases, one-click apps, cron jobs, full Admin Ops guest tools.
- **Files** — the customer file manager (`ServerFileBrowser`), opened only after an audited reason (`admin.server.files_open`); individual file operations are not separately audited (they go through the customer file API).
- **Backups** — schedule (audited change), platform/off-site coverage for this VMID from the backup status files, archives with audited restore (typed hostname), backup-now, backup/restore job list.
- **Game** (game servers) — `GameRuntimeCard` (unchanged), deep links into the customer game panel (settings, mods, players, console, worlds, schedules — the customer page lets an ADMIN view any server), players online + recent sessions, mods, config (secrets hidden), schedules.
- **Transfer / Move** — every node as a candidate with REAL numbers: committed RAM now→after vs `capacityRamMB`, live free RAM after the move vs the engine's 4 GB reserve, the platform pinned-RAM guard (`ramGuardVerdict`; blocking only when `NXEON_RAM_GUARD=enforce`), same-region (and same network) rule for dedicated IPs (`lib/admin-server/move-targets.ts`, pure + tested, mirrors `lib/vm-move/plan.ts`). The engine's safety guarantees are stated on the page. Dry run renders the engine's full `MovePlan` (checks, downtime + full-copy estimate, what changes); run (typed hostname + reason + accept dropped snapshots), rollback (only before commit), cleanup (forced before the 7-day keep window) and history with phase progress + log. **Wired through `lib/admin-server/vm-move-bridge.ts`**: the engine (`lib/vm-move/*`) is on unmerged branch `feature/vm-node-migration`, so on main the bridge returns "engine not enabled" and the page says so. Integration = set `ENGINE_PRESENT = true` and point the five bridge functions at `@/lib/vm-move/actions` (identical shapes). Even then, real runs stay off until `VM_MOVE_UI_ENABLED=1` (dry runs only need the engine; sandbox never runs).
- **Billing** — term/expiry/dunning/grace/lifetime spend, extend (existing `adminExtendServer` gifted-days logic), renew now (existing quote/split preview), free toggle, locked (grandfathered) price form, add-ons with live prices, card health (cards + unusable flags, re-add email, extend grace), invoices for this server, refund/adjust (`RefundControls`, bound to the latest term invoice), Admin Ops customer card (credit/extend/free/transfer ownership with reasons).
- **Activity** — 30-day uptime bars (`ServerUptimeDaily`), 7-day guest-RAM chart (`ServerMemSample`, downsampled), jobs timeline (progress, attempts, run time, error/payload), audit log rows naming the server (target / id / hostname, with impersonation attribution), guest telemetry events.
- **Danger** — suspend, ownership transfer (link), delete with a **"what will be destroyed" manifest** (`lib/admin-server/delete-manifest.ts` mirrors the worker DELETE job: VM `--purge` incl. attached volumes + snapshots, dedicated IP released, forwards, subdomain, GSLT; archive row kept; backups NOT deleted; no refund), warnings (running, paid days left, volumes), typed hostname + reason (`adminDeleteServer` → `serverAction("delete")`). Never one click.

### Servers list — `/admin/servers`
Server-side filtering + pagination (25/50/100) through one pure module, `lib/admin-server/fleet-query.ts` (URL ⇄ filters ⇄ Prisma where, tested), shared with the CSV route. Search: hostname, label, name, private IP, dedicated IP, subdomain, VMID, SSH port, server id, owner email/name. Filters: status, node, region, VPS/any game/game family, plan (VPS or game plan), expiring ≤N days, flagged (suspended / dunning / open abuse alert), mismatch (ERROR, stuck transitional, game down with run intent, or flagged by the latest drift scan). Sort: created/expires/hostname/status/vmid. Per-row health dot (`evaluateStateTruth` with one `/qemu` call per node on the page), live CPU, latest guest RAM/disk sample (one `DISTINCT ON` query per page), price via `serverFleetPriceCents`, tags, endpoint, owner (+ owner filter). Client table (`components/admin/server360/FleetTable.tsx`): selection with **safe bulk only** (reconcile, diagnose, export selected; power/delete link to Ops → Fleet), column chooser and saved views (per-browser localStorage; views are just named querystrings). CSV: `GET /api/admin/servers/export` (fleet area, refused while impersonating, ≤5000 rows, formula-injection-safe cells, audited `admin.fleet.export`). Archive views (cancelled/expired/deleted) unchanged.

### Customer 360 — `/admin/users/[id]`
Header (flags, risk level, quick credit/impersonate/message) + KPI strip + tabs:
- **Profile & risk** — client info (as before + billing country/VAT, Stripe customer, linked logins, teams), **flags** (`#flag:<kind>` CustomerNotes — no schema change; fraud watch, VIP, chargeback history, abuse history, do-not-refund, manual review), **risk signals** (`lib/admin-client/risk.ts`, pure + tested; facts loaded in `components/admin/client360/core.ts`): prior fraud audit rows, chargebacks (`partner.chargeback` rows on this customer's invoices), ≥3 cards (high if within 72 h — the pslgaming pattern), declined cards, billing country never seen in sign-ins, many countries, gmail-dot/+tag alias accounts, shared browser cookie (Visit.visitorId), shared IPs, refund ratio, create-and-delete churn, open abuse alerts, fast first purchase on a new account. The level is signal weight, explicitly not a fraud probability. Notes (existing component).
- **Servers** — cards with health, add-on badges, renewal/price/endpoint, reboot/suspend; hosting, email, domains, past servers (archive).
- **Billing** — wallet (+auto-recharge/spend cap), cards + health + re-add email, per-server subscriptions with locked vs live price, dunning, grace, ledger, invoices, refunds/adjustments (billing area), money-action audit trail.
- **Support** — tickets, DMs, live chats, email engagement + full `EmailLogViewer`.
- **Activity & security** — posture (2FA, backup codes, verification, session version), sessions (`UserSession`), sign-in/security events, IPs, API tokens + keys, recent pages, account activity (impersonation-attributed), staff actions targeting the customer.
- **Partner & referrals** — referral code/referrer/earnings, partner account or attachment, commissions, referrals, affiliate payouts.
- **Actions** (ADMIN) — credit, revenue exclude, impersonate, suspend, email password reset, resend verification, sign out everywhere, reset 2FA (typed email), merge **preview** (execution not built — says so), delete account (stricter than self-service GDPR delete: nothing owned, zero wallet, no open invoices, typed email + `DELETE` + reason).
The clients list gained state chips (suspended / unverified / 2FA on / flagged), flag + unverified badges, and search by customer id or any of their servers' hostname / IP.

### Server actions (all new)
`lib/actions-admin-server.ts` and `lib/actions-admin-client.ts`: every export opens with `gate()` (= `requireArea` + `assertNotImpersonating`; client actions also require ADMIN), zod validation, reason (4–300), per-admin in-memory rate limit, optional idempotency key (`claimOnce`), AuditLog row (`category` server/client, `target` id, IP), and reuses the existing action/job path for the real work. Guarded structurally by `test/admin-server-360.test.ts` (31 tests incl. logic).

### Not done / limits (honest)
- VM move run/rollback/cleanup are inert until the engine branch merges (see above).
- Admin comp-resize, rescue mode, account merge execution: not built.
- File-manager operations are audited at "opened with reason" granularity only.
- The NAT card does not read the node's live iptables chain (Diagnose does).
- Saved views / column choice are per browser (localStorage), not shared between admins.
"""
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
grep -c 'Admin server & customer pages redesign' docs/DOCUMENTATION.md

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

**Server detail page** (`/admin/servers/[id]?tab=…`), only the open tab loads:
- **Overview:** the database, Proxmox and game-runtime state side by side, with each mismatch listed and the existing one-click fix next to it. Also placement, plan, live stats, owner, billing summary, quick actions.
- **Network:** IPs and reverse DNS; the existing assign/release/switch-to-NAT IP tools with dry run and typed IP; port forwards with add/remove and conflict warnings; NAT chain card with resync; subdomain and DNS; platform firewall; guest firewall read-only.
- **Access:** SSH details, root-password reveal (needs a reason; logged who/when/IP, never the password), password reset, SSH keys, SSH login history, console, impersonate.
- **Compute:** power, live VM config, the memory pinning status, snapshots (typed name to roll back or delete), volumes, reinstall (typed hostname).
- **Software:** read-only discovery (Docker/compose, failed services, processes, ports), common services start/stop/restart, websites, SSL, databases, apps, cron.
- **Files:** the customer file manager, opened only after a logged reason.
- **Backups:** schedule, off-site coverage for this VM, restore (typed hostname), back up now.
- **Game:** existing runtime card, links into the game panel, players online, mods, config.
- **Transfer / Move:** every node with real capacity numbers (committed and live RAM, the RAM guard, same-region rule for dedicated IPs), dry-run plan, run / rollback / cleanup, history.
- **Billing:** extend (existing gifted-days logic), renew now, free toggle, locked price, add-ons, card health, refunds, ownership transfer.
- **Activity:** job timeline, audit log, uptime and memory charts.
- **Danger:** suspend, and delete with a "what will be destroyed" list plus typed hostname and reason.

**Servers list:** search by hostname, IP, VMID, port or owner email; filters for node, region, status, game, plan, expiring, flagged and mismatch; paging done on the server; a health dot per row; live CPU plus RAM/disk samples; column chooser; saved views (stored per browser); bulk actions limited to reconcile and diagnose; CSV export from the same filters.
